items.stem: To describe a rotation fully you must give
options: the centre and the mirror line
the centre, the angle and the direction
items.answer: the centre, the angle and the direction
items.markingKey: All three are needed (except for 180°, where direction is not needed).

items.stem: Explain why "a rotation of 90°" is not a full description of a transformation.
items.answer: It does not state the centre of rotation or the direction (clockwise or anticlockwise).
items.markingKey: B1 centre missing; B1 direction missing [2]

items.stem: A shape is reflected in the x-axis and then in the y-axis. Explain which single transformation has the same effect.
items.answer: (x, y) → (x, −y) → (−x, −y), which is a rotation of 180° about the origin.
items.markingKey: B1 working with coordinates; B1 rotation 180° about origin [2]

items.stem: Triangle T has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 3). Find the coordinates of the vertices of the image of T after a rotation of 180° about the origin.
items.markingKey: B2 all three vertices correct (B1 for two correct).

items.stem: Triangle T has vertices (2, 3), (5, 3) and (2, 5). Find the coordinates of the vertices of the image of T after a reflection in the line x = −2.
items.markingKey: B2 all three vertices correct (B1 for two correct).

items.stem: Triangle T has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1), (1, 4). Triangle A is the image of T after a reflection in the y-axis. Triangle B is the image of A after a reflection in the line y = x. (a) Write down the coordinates of the vertices of A. (b) Write down the coordinates of the vertices of B.
items.markingKey: (a) B2 (B1 for two correct) [2] (b) B2 (B1 for two correct) [2]

items.stem: To describe a translation fully you must give
items.answer: the column vector
items.markingKey: The vector gives the horizontal and vertical movement.

items.stem: Explain why the answer to a question asking for "a single transformation" must not describe two transformations.
items.answer: The question asks for one transformation that maps the object directly onto the image; a combination is not a single transformation and scores no marks.
items.markingKey: B1 one transformation required; B1 combinations not accepted [2]

items.stem: A triangle moves 2 units right and 3 units down. Aisha writes the translation vector as (−3, 2). Explain the error and give the correct vector.
items.answer: The top number is the horizontal movement and the bottom is the vertical movement: (2, −3).
items.markingKey: B1 order of components; B1 (2, −3) [2]

items.stem: Shape P is mapped onto shape Q by a reflection in the y-axis followed by a reflection in the x-axis. Lucas says the single transformation is "a reflection in both axes". Explain why this is not acceptable and give the correct single transformation.
items.answer: A single transformation is required. (x, y) → (−x, y) → (−x, −y), which is a rotation of 180° about the origin.
items.markingKey: B1 not a single transformation; B1 rotation 180° about (0, 0) [2]

items.stem: Triangle A has vertices (2, 1), (3, 1), (1, 3). Triangle B has vertices (−1, 2), (−1, 3), (−3, 1) (in the same order). Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle A onto triangle B.
items.answer: Rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin
items.markingKey: B1 rotation; B1 centre; B1 angle and direction.

items.stem: Triangle A has vertices (2, 1), (4, 1), (1, 3). Triangle B has vertices (−6, 1), (−8, 1), (−5, 3) (in the same order). Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle A onto triangle B.
items.answer: Reflection in the line x = −2
items.markingKey: B1 type of transformation; B1 full details (mirror line / vector).

items.stem: Triangle T has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1), (1, 2). Triangle A is the image of T after a reflection in the y-axis. Triangle B is the image of A after a reflection in the line y = x. (a) Describe fully the single transformation that maps T onto B. (b) Explain why T and B are congruent.
items.answer: (a) Rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin (b) Reflections (and rotations) do not change lengths or angles, so the image has the same size and shape.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 type; B1 or B2 full details [3] (b) B1 [1]

items.stem: Triangle T has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1), (1, 2). Triangle A is the image of T after a reflection in the y-axis. Triangle B is the image of A after a reflection in the line y = x. (a) Write down the coordinates of the vertices of A. (b) Write down the coordinates of the vertices of B. (c) Explain why T and B are congruent.
items.answer: (a) (−1, 1), (−3, 1), (−1, 2) (b) (1, −1), (1, −3), (2, −1) (c) Reflections (and rotations) do not change lengths or angles, so the image has the same size and shape.
items.markingKey: (a) B2 (B1 for two correct) [2] (b) B2 (B1 for two correct) [2] (c) B1 [1]

items.stem: A shape is enlarged by scale factor 3. By what factor is its area multiplied?
items.markingKey: Area scale factor = (length scale factor)².

items.stem: Explain why an enlargement with scale factor ½ is still called an enlargement even though the shape gets smaller.
items.answer: In mathematics an enlargement is any transformation where lengths are multiplied by the same scale factor from a centre; a factor between 0 and 1 gives a smaller image.
items.markingKey: B1 definition; B1 factor < 1 gives reduction [2]

items.stem: Explain how to find the centre of an enlargement from an object and its image on a grid.
items.answer: Draw straight lines through corresponding vertices of the object and image; the centre is where these lines meet.
items.markingKey: B1 join corresponding points; B1 intersection is centre [2]

items.stem: Triangle T has vertices (3, 2), (7, 2), (3, 4). T is enlarged with scale factor 1/3 and centre (1, 0). Find the coordinates of the vertices of the image.
items.markingKey: M1 vector from centre × scale factor; A1 one vertex correct; A2 all three vertices (A1 two).

items.stem: Triangle T has vertices (1, 1), (5, 1), (1, 3). T is enlarged with scale factor 1/2 and centre (−1, −1). Find the coordinates of the vertices of the image.
items.markingKey: M1 vector from centre × scale factor; A1 one vertex correct; A2 all three vertices (A1 two).

items.stem: Triangle P has vertices (2, 3), (6, 3), (2, 6). P is enlarged with scale factor 2, centre (0, 2), to give triangle Q. (a) Calculate the area of Q. (b) Calculate the length of the longest side of Q.
items.answer: (a) 24 square units (b) 10.0 units
items.markingKey: (a) M1 × (2)²; A1 [2] (b) M1 longest side of P = 5; A1 × 2 [2]

items.stem: An enlargement has scale factor ½. What happens to the lengths of the shape?
items.answer: They are halved
items.markingKey: A fractional scale factor between 0 and 1 makes the image smaller.

items.stem: Explain how an enlargement with scale factor −1 is related to a rotation.
items.answer: Scale factor −1 maps each point to the opposite side of the centre at the same distance, which is the same as a rotation of 180° about the centre.
items.markingKey: B1 same distance opposite side; B1 rotation 180° [2]

items.stem: A shape with area 12 cm² is enlarged by scale factor 4. Noah says the area of the image is 48 cm². Explain the error and find the correct area.
items.answer: Area is multiplied by the square of the scale factor (16), so the area is 192 cm².
items.markingKey: B1 area factor k²; B1 192 cm² [2]

items.stem: A shape with area 10 cm² is enlarged by scale factor 2. Amara says the area of the image is 20 cm². Explain the error and find the correct area.
items.answer: Area is multiplied by the square of the scale factor (4), so the area is 40 cm².
items.markingKey: B1 area factor k²; B1 40 cm² [2]

items.stem: Triangle T has vertices (0, 0), (4, 0), (0, 2). T is enlarged with scale factor 1/3 and centre (−2, −2). Find the coordinates of the vertices of the image.
items.markingKey: M1 vector from centre × scale factor; A1 one vertex correct; A2 all three vertices (A1 two).

items.stem: Triangle T has vertices (0, 2), (4, 2), (0, 4). T is enlarged with scale factor 3 and centre (−2, 0). Find the coordinates of the vertices of the image.
items.markingKey: M1 vector from centre × scale factor; A1 one vertex correct; A2 all three vertices (A1 two).

items.stem: Triangle P has vertices (4, −1), (8, −1), (4, 2). P is enlarged with scale factor 3, centre (2, −2), to give triangle Q. (a) Calculate the area of Q. (b) Calculate the length of the longest side of Q.
items.answer: (a) 54 square units (b) 15.0 units
items.markingKey: (a) M1 × (3)²; A1 [2] (b) M1 longest side of P = 5; A1 × 3 [2]

items.stem: Triangle P has vertices (0, 2), (4, 2), (0, 5). P is enlarged with scale factor −2, centre (−2, 1), to give triangle Q. (a) Calculate the length of the longest side of Q. (b) Describe fully the single transformation that maps Q back onto P.
items.answer: (a) 10.0 units (b) Enlargement, scale factor −1/2, centre (−2, 1)
items.markingKey: (a) M1 longest side of P = 5; A1 × 2 [2] (b) B1 enlargement; B1 scale factor; B1 centre [3]

items.stem: a = (3, −2) and b = (1, 4) are column vectors. What is a + b?
items.markingKey: Add the components: 3 + 1 = 4, −2 + 4 = 2.

items.stem: Explain why the vectors (2, 3) and (6, 9) are parallel.
items.answer: (6, 9) = 3 × (2, 3), so one is a scalar multiple of the other and they have the same direction.
items.markingKey: B1 scalar multiple; B1 conclusion [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between the vectors AB and BA.
items.answer: They have the same length but opposite directions: BA = −AB.
items.markingKey: B1 same magnitude; B1 opposite direction [2]

items.stem: Show whether the vectors (3, 1) and (6, 2) are parallel.
items.markingKey: M1 compares ratios of components; A1 conclusion.

items.stem: a = (0, −5), b = (5, −1) and c = (15, −23). Find the values of m and n such that ma + nb = c.
items.markingKey: M1 5n = 15 and −5m − n = −23; M1 solve; A1 A1.

items.stem: O is the origin. A and B are points with OA = a = (1, −3) and OB = b = (5, 1). (a) Find 2a − b as a column vector. (b) C is the point such that OC = a + b. Explain what type of quadrilateral OACB is.
items.answer: (a) (−3, −7) (b) A parallelogram, since AC = b = OB and BC = a = OA.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 B1 [2] (b) B1 parallelogram; B1 reason [2]

items.stem: In column vector form, a = (2, −5) and b = (−3, 4). Find 3a − 2b.
Explain what a negative scalar multiple, such as −2a, represents.
items.answer: A vector twice as long as a but in the opposite direction.
items.markingKey: B1 length doubled; B1 opposite direction [2]

items.stem: a = (5, −1) and b = (−4, −4). Nadia calculates 2a − 3b = (22, −14). Explain the error and find the correct answer.
items.answer: Each component must be found as 2 × (a component) − 3 × (b component): 2a − 3b = (22, 10).
items.markingKey: B1 identifies sign/component error; B1 (22, 10) [2]

items.stem: a = (−5, −2) and b = (3, −1) are column vectors. Write 4a + 3b as a column vector.
a = (0, −2) and b = (1, −1) are column vectors. Write 3a − 3b as a column vector.
A is the point (−3, −1) and B is the point (5, 3). Write AB as a column vector, and find the coordinates of C where BC = AB.

O is the origin. A and B are points with OA = a = (0, 4) and OB = b = (5, 0). (a) Find the coordinates of the midpoint M of AB. (b) Find 2a − b as a column vector. (c) Find the value of k for which ka + b is parallel to the x-axis.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 a + ½AB; A1 [2] (b) B1 B1 [2] (c) M1 y-component = 0; A1 [2]

items.stem: What is the magnitude of the vector (3, 4)?
Explain how vectors can be used to show that three points A, B and C lie on a straight line.
items.answer: Show that AB is a scalar multiple of AC (or BC); then the lines are parallel and share the point A, so the points are collinear.
items.markingKey: B1 scalar multiple; B1 common point [2]

items.stem: Explain why the magnitude of a vector can never be negative.
items.answer: It is a length, found from √(x² + y²), and a square root of a sum of squares is never negative.
items.markingKey: B1 length; B1 √ of squares ≥ 0 [2]

items.stem: OA = a, OB = b and OC = −2a + 3b. Show that A, B and C lie on a straight line.
items.answer: AB = b − a and AC = −3a + 3b = 3(b − a) = 3AB, so AC is parallel to AB and they share point A.
items.markingKey: M1 AB = b − a; M1 AC = OC − OA; A1 AC = 3AB with conclusion (common point A).

items.stem: OA = a and OB = b. P lies on AB such that AP : PB = 1 : 4. Find OP in terms of a and b, in its simplest form.
items.answer: ⅘a + ⅕b
items.markingKey: M1 OP = OA + 1/5AB; M1 a + 1/5(b − a); A1 ⅘a + ⅕b.

items.stem: OA = a and OB = b. P lies on AB such that AP : PB = 1 : 2. Find OP in terms of a and b, in its simplest form.
items.answer: ⅔a + ⅓b
items.markingKey: M1 OP = OA + 1/3AB; M1 a + 1/3(b − a); A1 ⅔a + ⅓b.

items.stem: OABC is a parallelogram with OA = a and OC = c. M is the midpoint of AB. P lies on the diagonal OB such that OP : PB = 1 : 3. (a) Find OP in terms of a and c. (b) Find CM in terms of a and c.
items.answer: (a) ¼a + ¼c (b) a − ½c

items.stem: OABC is a parallelogram with OA = a and OC = c. M is the midpoint of AB. P lies on the diagonal OB such that OP : PB = 1 : 2. (a) Find OB in terms of a and c. (b) Find OM in terms of a and c. (c) Given that a = (4, 0) and c = (2, 6), find |OB|.
items.answer: (a) a + c (b) a + ½c (c) 8.49

items.stem: O is the origin, OA = a and OB = b. Which vector is AB?
items.answer: b − a
items.markingKey: AB = AO + OB = −a + b.

items.stem: M is the midpoint of AB, where OA = a and OB = b. What is OM?
items.answer: ½(a + b)
items.markingKey: OM = a + ½(b − a) = ½(a + b).

items.stem: Explain why |a + b| is usually not equal to |a| + |b|.
items.answer: The vectors form two sides of a triangle; the third side is shorter than the sum of the other two unless a and b are in the same direction.
items.markingKey: B1 triangle inequality; B1 equal only if same direction [2]

items.stem: Omar says the magnitude of (−6, 8) is √(−6 + 8) = √2. Explain the error and find the correct magnitude.
items.answer: Magnitude uses Pythagoras: √((−6)² + 8²) = √100 = 10.
items.markingKey: B1 must square components; B1 10 [2]

items.stem: OAB is a triangle with OA = a and OB = b. M is the midpoint of AB. Find, in terms of a and b, (a) AB (b) AM (c) OM, giving each in its simplest form.
items.answer: (a) b − a (b) ½b − ½a (c) ½a + ½b
items.markingKey: (a) B1 (b) B1 (c) M1 OA + AM; A1.

items.stem: OA = a, OB = b and OC = −a + 2b. Show that A, B and C lie on a straight line.
items.answer: AB = b − a and AC = −2a + 2b = 2(b − a) = 2AB, so AC is parallel to AB and they share point A.
items.markingKey: M1 AB = b − a; M1 AC = OC − OA; A1 AC = 2AB with conclusion (common point A).

items.stem: OA = a and OB = b. P lies on AB such that AP : PB = 2 : 3. Find OP in terms of a and b, in its simplest form.
items.answer: ⅗a + ⅖b
items.markingKey: M1 OP = OA + 2/5AB; M1 a + 2/5(b − a); A1 ⅗a + ⅖b.

items.stem: OA = a and OB = b. P lies on AB such that AP : PB = 3 : 1. Find OP in terms of a and b, in its simplest form.
items.answer: ¼a + ¾b
items.markingKey: M1 OP = OA + 3/4AB; M1 a + 3/4(b − a); A1 ¼a + ¾b.

items.stem: OABC is a parallelogram with OA = a and OC = c. M is the midpoint of AB. P lies on the diagonal OB such that OP : PB = 1 : 3. (a) Find OB in terms of a and c. (b) Given that a = (4, 0) and c = (2, 6), find |OB|.
OABC is a parallelogram with OA = a and OC = c. M is the midpoint of AB. P lies on the diagonal OB such that OP : PB = 2 : 3. (a) Find OB in terms of a and c. (b) Find CM in terms of a and c.
items.answer: (a) a + c (b) a − ½c

items.stem: To describe a reflection fully you must give

items.answer: the equation of the mirror line
items.markingKey: For example "reflection in the line y = 2".

items.stem: A triangle moves 4 units right and 4 units up. Sofia writes the translation vector as (4, 4). Explain the error and give the correct vector.
items.answer: The top number is the horizontal movement and the bottom is the vertical movement: (4, 4).
items.markingKey: B1 order of components; B1 (4, 4) [2]

items.stem: Triangle T has vertices (2, 2), (4, 2) and (2, 6). Find the coordinates of the vertices of the image of T after a rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin.
items.markingKey: B2 all three vertices correct (B1 for two correct).

items.stem: Triangle T has vertices (3, 3), (7, 3) and (3, 5). Find the coordinates of the vertices of the image of T after a rotation of 180° about (2, 1).

(a) Describe fully the single transformation that maps T onto B. (b) Triangle C has vertices (−5, 6), (−3, 6), (−5, 9). Describe fully the single transformation that maps T onto C.
items.answer: (a) Rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin (b) Translation by the vector (−6, 5)
items.markingKey: (a) B1 type; B1 or B2 full details [3] (b) B1 translation; B1 vector [2]

items.stem: An enlargement with a negative scale factor produces an image that is
options: on the opposite side of the centre and upside down
on the same side and the same way up
items.answer: on the opposite side of the centre and upside down
items.markingKey: Each point moves through the centre to the other side.

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Explain how to find the centre of an enlargement from an object and its image on a grid. (b) Explain how an enlargement with scale factor −1 is related to a rotation.

items.stem: Triangle P has vertices (2, 3), (6, 3), (2, 6). P is enlarged with scale factor 2, centre (0, 2), to give triangle Q. (a) Calculate the area of P. (b) Calculate the length of the longest side of Q. (c) Describe fully the single transformation that maps Q back onto P.

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Two vectors are parallel if (b) If AB = a, what is BA?
items.answer: (a) one is a scalar multiple of the other (b) −a
items.markingKey: (a) For example 2a + 4b is parallel to a + 2b. (b) Reversing the direction changes the sign.

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain why the vectors (2, 3) and (6, 9) are parallel. (b) Explain what a negative scalar multiple, such as −2a, represents.

items.stem: A is the point (−4, 1) and B is the point (0, 1). Write AB as a column vector, and find the coordinates of C where BC = AB.

O is the origin. A and B are points with OA = a = (0, −4) and OB = b = (5, −3). (a) C is the point such that OC = a + b. Explain what type of quadrilateral OACB is. (b) Find the value of k for which ka + b is parallel to the x-axis.
items.answer: (a) A parallelogram, since AC = b = OB and BC = a = OA. (b) k = −3/4

items.stem: Triangle T has vertices (4, 0), (8, 0), (4, 2). T is enlarged with scale factor 5/2 and centre (2, −2). Find the coordinates of the vertices of the image.
items.markingKey: M1 vector from centre × scale factor; A1 one vertex correct; A2 all three vertices (A1 two).

items.stem: Triangle P has vertices (0, 3), (4, 3), (0, 6). P is enlarged with scale factor 3, centre (−2, 2), to give triangle Q. (a) Find the coordinates of the vertices of Q. (b) Describe fully the single transformation that maps Q back onto P.
items.answer: (a) (4, 5), (16, 5), (4, 14) (b) Enlargement, scale factor 1/3, centre (−2, 2)
items.markingKey: (a) M1; A2 [3] (b) B1 enlargement; B1 scale factor; B1 centre [3]

items.stem: In column vector form, a = (3, −6) and b = (6, 3). Find 3a − b.
Answer both parts. (a) Explain the difference between the vectors AB and BA. (b) Explain why the vectors (2, 3) and (6, 9) are parallel.
items.answer: (a) They have the same length but opposite directions: BA = −AB. (b) (6, 9) = 3 × (2, 3), so one is a scalar multiple of the other and they have the same direction.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 same magnitude; B1 opposite direction [2] (b) B1 scalar multiple; B1 conclusion [2]

items.stem: A is the point (0, 1) and B is the point (2, 5). Write AB as a column vector, and find the coordinates of C where BC = AB.

O is the origin. A and B are points with OA = a = (4, 5) and OB = b = (−4, −4). (a) C is the point such that OC = a + b. Explain what type of quadrilateral OACB is. (b) Find the value of k for which ka + b is parallel to the x-axis.
items.answer: (a) A parallelogram, since AC = b = OB and BC = a = OA. (b) k = 4/5
items.markingKey: (a) B1 parallelogram; B1 reason [2] (b) M1 y-component = 0; A1 [2]

items.stem: Yusuf says the magnitude of (−3, 4) is √(−3 + 4) = √1. Explain the error and find the correct magnitude.
items.answer: Magnitude uses Pythagoras: √((−3)² + 4²) = √25 = 5.
items.markingKey: B1 must square components; B1 5 [2]

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain why |a + b| is usually not equal to |a| + |b|. (b) Explain why the magnitude of a vector can never be negative.
items.answer: (a) The vectors form two sides of a triangle; the third side is shorter than the sum of the other two unless a and b are in the same direction. (b) It is a length, found from √(x² + y²), and a square root of a sum of squares is never negative.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 triangle inequality; B1 equal only if same direction [2] (b) B1 length; B1 √ of squares ≥ 0 [2]

items.stem: Ines says the magnitude of (−5, 12) is √(−5 + 12) = √7. Explain the error and find the correct magnitude.
items.answer: Magnitude uses Pythagoras: √((−5)² + 12²) = √169 = 13.
items.markingKey: B1 must square components; B1 13 [2]

items.stem: OA = a and OB = b. P lies on AB such that AP : PB = 1 : 3. Find OP in terms of a and b, in its simplest form.
items.answer: ¾a + ¼b
items.markingKey: M1 OP = OA + 1/4AB; M1 a + 1/4(b − a); A1 ¾a + ¼b.

items.stem: OABC is a parallelogram with OA = a and OC = c. M is the midpoint of AB. P lies on the diagonal OB such that OP : PB = 2 : 1. (a) Find CM in terms of a and c. (b) Given that a = (4, 0) and c = (2, 6), find |OB|.
